answer: Summit benchmark proof — $43 buys one brass survey disk per identity, set in a named summit's cairn, its elevation published by the county surveyor. Each epoch the holder files a fresh GPS fix at the disk; a fix off by a hand's breadth is struck, and a second filing on the same disk cancels the pair. The disk sits in karst limestone, which dissolves, sinking the disk a little each year, so a fix copied from last epoch no longer matches. The timber crew below stamps the same disk number on every load ticket, so an identity with no disk has no timber and no summit to stand on.
